body: Two internal contradictions worth flagging. First, the pruning heuristic in FR-004 prunes exactly the wrong skills: it removes an unused skill only when it is DISSIMILAR from everything else (min cosine similarity < 0.70), which means it deletes unique capabilities and retains the redundant ones. A curation mechanism meant to combat 'retrieval noise and state bloat from overlapping skills' should remove skills that are highly similar to a retained neighbor, not maximally distinct ones. As written, the intervention could degrade the library's coverage while leaving redundancy intact — and any 'performance recovery' it measures would be an artifact of the inverted criterion. Second, FR-005 asks for a piecewise linear breakpoint (x0) fit to four library sizes (10, 30, 50, 100). A single-breakpoint model estimated from four design points is essentially underdetermined — the breakpoint location will be driven by whichever of the two interior points happens to fall below the fitted line, with no way to distinguish a genuine tipping point from noise. The expected-results narrative in the project description even anticipates a non-monotonic (plateau-then-decline) curve, which a single-breakpoint piecewise linear model cannot represent. Either more library sizes or a different model class is needed before SC-004's 'tipping point' can be called established rather than asserted. A lesser note: FR-007's VIF check on 'library size' and 'total redundancy' is computed over a 4-point design; VIF from four observations and two predictors is nearly meaningless as a collinearity diagnostic.
